_llm_instructions._about: This block is documentation for any LLM asked to UPDATE or VET this file. The runtime app ignores it. Preserve this block verbatim when you output a revised file — do not edit, summarize, reorder, or remove it.
_llm_instructions.purpose: This file drives a patient-facing visit-prep tool. The runtime app reads `items` to surface preventive-care topics and to generate a research prompt that the patient takes to OpenEvidence and to their clinician. It is NOT medical advice.
your_job: Read this entire _llm_instructions block first. Do not skim.

Use the deepest research mode available to you (deep research, web search, peer-reviewed and guideline-body sources). Do NOT answer from memory — preventive-care guidelines change, sometimes annually.
Cross-check every item against the current published version of its cited source. Verify age ranges, sex restrictions, intervals, modifiers (family history, smoking, etc.), and the source_year.
VET mode: confirm each item is still correct as-is. Flag drift in review_notes with one line per affected item.
UPDATE mode: add, remove, reword, or reorder items as evidence warrants. Document every change in review_notes with a one-line reason naming the source guideline.
Set last_reviewed to today's date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Set reviewer to identify yourself or your process.
Preserve this _llm_instructions block VERBATIM in your output. It must travel with the file forever.
Output the complete JSON file only. No markdown fences. No commentary before or after. No trailing text. Valid parseable JSON.

schema.schema_version: string, semver-ish (bump on breaking field changes)
schema.reviewer: string identifying the human or process
schema.review_notes: string summarizing what changed in this revision
schema.category_order: array of category keys, top-to-bottom display order
schema.category_labels: map from category key to patient-readable label
schema.sources: map from source short-name to canonical URL
schema.items: array of recommendation objects (see item_schema below)
schema._design_proposal_v1_2: internal governance proposal — do not promote to live schema until resolved

item_schema.title: patient-readable title, <= 60 chars
item_schema.source: USPSTF | ACIP/CDC | ACC-AHA | ADA | KDIGO | AUA | NCCN | combinations
item_schema.source_year: YYYY of the cited published recommendation version
item_schema.eligibility: clause (see clause_grammar) — gates whether the item applies at all
item_schema.priority_when: clause group ({any_of:[...]} or {all_of:[...]}) — when matched, triggers the 'especially relevant' visual highlight
item_schema.discussion: 1-2 sentences, plain language, ~8th-grade reading level. Always framed as something to discuss with a clinician. Never tells the patient what to do.

clause_grammar.description: A clause is an object. All present keys must match (logical AND within one clause).

keys.all_of: array of clauses (logical AND across them)
keys.any_of: array of clauses (logical OR across them)

clause_grammar.top_level_note: A top-level priority_when MUST be wrapped in {any_of:[...]} or {all_of:[...]}.

categorization_rules.cancer: Any cancer screening (lung, colon, breast, cervical, prostate, skin/melanoma, etc.)
categorization_rules.cardiometabolic: Cardiovascular, diabetes, kidney, lipid, bone, vascular (BP, lipids, A1c, kidney protection, osteoporosis, AAA)
categorization_rules.infection: Communicable-disease screening and immunization (HIV, Hep C, STI, vaccinations)
categorization_rules.lifestyle: Behavioral and mental health (tobacco cessation, alcohol screening, depression screening, sleep)

_llm_instructions.ordering_rule: Within each category, place items in DESCENDING order of expected population health benefit = impact × prevalence × strength of evidence in the general U.S. adult population. Justify any reorder in review_notes.

policies.approval_fields: approved_by_openevidence and approved_by_cmi_committee must be present on every item. Set approved=false until formally validated, with when='' and explanation noting why pending. When approved=true, include the date and a one-sentence explanation of what was checked.
policies.discussion_field: 1-2 sentences, plain language, ~8th-grade reading level. Frame as something to discuss with a clinician. Never instruct the patient.
policies.patient_safety: If a recommendation depends on missing data, the runtime app will surface that. Do not invent eligibility logic to compensate — the prompt asks the LLM downstream to flag missing data points.

output_contract: Return the complete, valid, parseable JSON file.
Preserve this _llm_instructions block verbatim at the top.
Update last_reviewed to today, reviewer to identify yourself.
Update review_notes with a one-line entry per change, citing the source guideline.
No markdown fences, no commentary, no trailing text. JSON only.

review_notes: v1.3: moved deep LLM update/vet instructions to top of file as _llm_instructions (self-describing — travels with the file). Removed duplicate build_prompt from _design_proposal_v1_2.

items.title: Colon cancer screening
items.discussion: Discuss modality (stool tests vs colonoscopy) and interval. Family history may move start age earlier.

items.title: Breast cancer screening (mammogram)
items.discussion: Current USPSTF recommends biennial mammography 40–74 for average risk. Family history may change timing.

items.title: Lung cancer screening (low-dose CT)
items.discussion: Annual LDCT for 50–80 with ≥20 pack-years if currently smoking or quit within 15 years.

items.title: Prostate cancer screening (shared decision)
items.discussion: PSA is preference-sensitive. Black men and those with family history may be encouraged to start earlier discussion.

items.title: Cervical cancer screening (Pap / HPV)
items.discussion: Cytology, HPV, or co-testing depending on age — confirm interval and most recent result.

items.title: Skin / melanoma vigilance
items.discussion: Discuss warning signs (ABCDE) and whether routine skin exams make sense given your risk.

items.title: Blood pressure check & target discussion
items.discussion: Confirm proper technique, consider home BP log, and discuss target based on overall risk.

items.title: Lipid panel & ASCVD risk
items.discussion: Discuss LDL goals (different for primary vs secondary prevention) and whether statins are appropriate.

items.title: Diabetes / prediabetes screening
items.discussion: Confirm whether HbA1c or fasting glucose is appropriate; discuss prevention if prediabetic.

items.title: Kidney protection (UACR, eGFR, BP targets)
items.discussion: Discuss UACR, eGFR, BP targets, and kidney-protective therapies (e.g., ACEi/ARB, SGLT2i if indicated).

items.title: Osteoporosis screening (DEXA)
items.discussion: Discuss DEXA timing and fall/fracture prevention. Earlier if other osteoporosis risk factors.

items.title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm screening (one-time)
items.discussion: One-time ultrasound for men 65–75 who have ever smoked.

items.title: Vaccinations (age-appropriate)
items.discussion: Confirm flu, COVID, Tdap; shingles (50+); pneumococcal (per ACIP); RSV (60+ per shared decision).

items.title: Hepatitis C screening (one-time)
items.discussion: Confirm whether you've ever been screened; one-time screening recommended for adults 18–79.

items.title: HIV screening (baseline)
items.discussion: Baseline screening for all adolescents and adults 15–65; repeat based on risk.

items.title: Chlamydia & STI screening
items.discussion: Annual screening for sexually active women under 25; risk-based screening for older women.

items.title: Tobacco cessation support
items.discussion: Behavioral support plus FDA-approved pharmacotherapy is the highest-leverage intervention for smokers.

items.title: Depression / mood screening
items.discussion: Use validated screen (e.g., PHQ-9) and discuss treatment options that improve function.

items.title: Unhealthy alcohol use screening
items.discussion: AUDIT-C or similar; brief counseling if positive.

_design_proposal_v1_2.summary: Adds a two-gate governance trail to every item: OpenEvidence validation + CMI committee approval, each with date and explanation. This block is documentation only — the runtime app does NOT read these fields yet. Schema and update instructions for LLMs now live at the top in _llm_instructions.
_design_proposal_v1_2.rationale: Patients act on the framing in this tool. As the JSON becomes the source of truth for what patients see, every recommendation should pass two review gates before being published. (1) OpenEvidence validation confirms the wording and source citation match current evidence. (2) CMI committee approval confirms clinical framing, tone, and patient-facing appropriateness. Both gates record date and a brief explanation so changes are auditable. An item with either gate unapproved should be hidden in production or flagged in the UI as 'pending review.'

approved_by_openevidence.explanation: Pending review against current OpenEvidence summary.

approved_by_cmi_committee.explanation: Pending CMI committee review of patient-facing wording.

open_questions: Should items missing approval be hidden, shown with a 'pending' badge, or shown normally with provenance available on tap?
Do approvals expire (e.g., re-review required every 12 months)? If so, the rules engine should treat stale approvals as not-approved.
Should we record reviewer initials on each approval, or is the committee-level record enough?
